content.answer: Fix rule: merge options by stable id, not by name — when updating a single-select field, pass every existing option object through unchanged (old name keeps its old id), assign fresh ids only to genuinely new names, and continue the id sequence from max(existing id)+1; rebuilding the option list from just the submitted names makes the API recreate all options with new ids, which silently clears the value references in every existing data row.
content.reuse_advice: For any update to an id-referenced catalog (single/multi-select fields, statuses, tags, enum dictionaries): never send a bare list of names as the full replacement. Always fetch the current catalog, diff by stable id — keep existing options as-is (original id + name), add only new entries with fresh ids continuing from max(existing id)+1, and remove or rename explicitly. Treating names as identity causes the system to rebuild the catalog with new ids and silently severs every existing row's reference to the old options.
